To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we can visualize compositionality in neural networks by plotting word embeddings; (2) we can quantify the salience of a unit by back-propagating the gradient of the loss function, measuring variance, and measuring the flow of information in LSTM-like gates; (3) we show that LSTMs out-perform simple recurrent nets by allowing more information flow through the network; (4) our methods are applicable to any neural model for NLP.
we can visualize compositionality and salience of units in neural models for sentiment analysis, and that LSTMs outperformed SRNs because they are better able to focus on salient words.

we have found four ways to visualize the salience of units in neural networks, that these visualizations are helpful for understanding compositionality in neural network models, that the salience of a unit in a recurrent net can be measured using backpropagation, the variance of a word from the average word unit, or the LSTM-style gates that are used to control information flow in the network, and that the salience measurements can be used to understand why LSTMs are more effective than simple recurrent nets.
